What is bought is all-up rounds, containers and trainers, i.e. the munition the line procures, and the appropriation agrees explicitly: $101,394,424 of fiscal 2023 and $183,097,105 of fiscal 2024 'Air Force procurement missile funding' against a missile-procurement line (lexicon_doc 410). The same designator sits on RDT&E element 0207327F; the announced procurement money resolves that collision to SDB002.

refute_a.reason: Fiscal 2023/2024 Air Force procurement MISSILE funding ($101,394,424 + $183,097,105) against a missile-procurement line buying Lot 10 all-up rounds, containers and trainers — the munition itself; the Navy weapons-procurement share is the partner service's portion of a joint buy and does not displace the Air Force line, and SMALL DIAMETER BOMB II is a single-weapon line.

refute_b.reason: The GBU-53 designator sits on two rows, but the asymmetry favours the proposal: the announcement says 'SDBII' and SDB002's own title is 'SMALL DIAMETER BOMB II', whereas the competing 0207327F row is the generic 'Small Diameter Bomb (SDB)' — and the object is a numbered production lot of all-up rounds, which is the procurement line's article; SDB000/GBU-39 is SDB I, a different weapon the announcement never names.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Predator (MQ1) and Reaper (MQ9) unmanned aerial systems contractor logistic support
proposals.rationale: Reject by design under §3 'generic services: ... logistics' — the follow-on year of the same contractor logistics support described in record 52, with the identical enumerated scope (program management, configuration management, depot repair, field maintenance) on fiscal 2016 Air Force and Air National Guard operations and maintenance funds. Platform-named sustainment services, not a program element's own work.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Global Positioning System (GPS) IIF on-orbit support to satisfy the GPS IIF mission requirements
proposals.rationale: Reject by design under §3 'generic services: engineering support', the companion case to record 2: 'engineering services to the operational units in support of GPS Block IIF satellite constellation'. The constellation is the platform the support sustains, and at least four codes in this index carry a GPS name (GPSSPC, GPS03C, GPSIII, SPCMOD), so even setting the generic-services pattern aside there is no way to say which line this would execute.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Reaper (MQ-9) contractor logistics support
proposals.rationale: Reject by design under §3 'generic services: ... logistics'. The scope is program management, field service representative support, depot repair and maintenance, sustaining engineering, supply and logistics, configuration management, tech data and software maintenance and warehouse support, funded with fiscal 2020 operations and maintenance money. The MQ-9 name identifies the platform being sustained, not a program 0205219F funds.

proposals.announcement_evidence: 15,000 Lot 20 Joint Direct Attack Munitions (JDAM) tailkits
proposals.rationale: The delivery order buys the article the line is named for: 15,000 Lot 20 JDAM tailkits, with the whole $325,821,749 obligated as fiscal 2016 MUNITIONS PROCUREMENT funds against 353620, whose title is simply 'Joint Direct Attack Munition' and which sits in the Air Force ammunition-procurement exhibit (lexicon_doc 409). Name, article and appropriation all agree, the munition is the program rather than a platform supporting it, and no other code in this org's index owns a JDAM name. The accompanying technical services and field support are incidental to a tail-kit buy, not the substance of the order.

refute_a.reason: The whole $325,821,749 is fiscal 2016 MUNITIONS PROCUREMENT money against an ammunition-procurement line titled 'Joint Direct Attack Munition', buying 15,000 Lot 20 JDAM tailkits; the technical services and field support ride along on a tail-kit delivery order rather than constituting it, so this is not O&M sustainment dressed as procurement.

refute_b.reason: 'The Joint Direct Attack Munition (JDAM)' is owned by exactly one row of F.tsv (353620), the announcement names the munition itself rather than a carrying platform or a contractor, and the only other tail-kit name in the index, 'Tail Kit Assembly (TKA)' on 354050, belongs to the B61-12 trainer — a program the announcement never mentions, so nothing here links equally well elsewhere.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the StormBreaker® Small Diameter Bomb Increment II (SDB II, GBU-53/B)
proposals.rationale: The GBU-53/B designator is present and unambiguous as a weapon, but this action is purely a ceiling increase — $275,000,000 to $600,000,000 — and 'No funds are being obligated at the time of award'. With no appropriation in the record, nothing distinguishes the missile-procurement line SDB002 from the RDT&E element 0207327F, both of which own the GBU-53 designator in this index. An IDIQ ceiling with no money is close to the §3 umbrella pattern; weak, not link.

proposals.announcement_evidence: digital beam forming multi-beam Common Data Link apertures
proposals.rationale: Reject by design under the §3 pattern that the named thing is something the contract merely uses rather than the program the PE funds. 'Common Data Link apertures' appears here as one component inside the technology list of a different program — MUDLAN, the Mobile Unmanned/Manned Distributed Lethality Airborne Network Joint Capabilities Technology Demonstration — and MUDLAN is not in this org's index at all. Linking the CDL Executive Agent line to a MUDLAN development award would attribute another program's money to it.

proposals.announcement_evidence: StormBreaker (SDBII, GBU-53/B) production Lot 9
proposals.rationale: The basic award of the contract whose Lot 10 modification is record 63: production Lot 9 of 'SDBII, GBU-53/B assembled weapons and containers'. 'GBU-53/B' normalizes to the index designator 'GBU-53' on SDB002 ('SMALL DIAMETER BOMB II'), the assembled weapons are the article that line procures, and $239,651,584 of fiscal 2023 Air Force procurement funding is obligated against a missile-procurement line (lexicon_doc 410). The RDT&E element 0207327F shares the designator; the announced procurement appropriation picks the procurement line.

refute_a.reason: Fiscal 2023 Air Force procurement funding of $239,651,584 against a missile-procurement line for 'SDBII, GBU-53/B assembled weapons and containers' — the assembled munition the line procures; production money, production line, no platform and no aggregate title.

refute_b.reason: Same two-owner designator as record 63 and the same tiebreak on identity grounds: the announcement's 'SDBII, GBU-53/B assembled weapons and containers' reproduces SDB002's own title 'SMALL DIAMETER BOMB II' and names Lot 9 of the article that line procures, while 0207327F's row is the generic SDB development name.

proposals.announcement_evidence: 308 Lot 20 Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile – Extended Range missiles with containers
proposals.rationale: The JASSM-ER name matches the index row exactly and the buy is unambiguous (308 Lot 20 missiles with containers), but the whole $318,933,722 is fiscal 2022 MISSILE PROCUREMENT money and 0207325F is the RDT&E element (lexicon_doc 412). As with records 33 and 45, the procurement alternative JASSM0 carries only 'AGM-158D' in this index, a different variant from the AGM-158B being bought, so no line here can take the attribution.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Joint Direct Attack Munition (JDAM) tail kits
proposals.rationale: The modification's stated content is JDAM tail kits — 'JDAM strap-on inertial guidance kits with the capability to receive guidance updates from global positioning systems to increase weapon accuracy for conventional inventory bombs' — which is the article 353620 procures, described in the line's own terms. Although the action is styled a ceiling increase, fiscal 2018 procurement funds of $919,429,166 are explicitly obligated, so this is not a §3 empty-ceiling paragraph: procurement money against the Air Force ammunition-procurement JDAM line (lexicon_doc 409). Same PIID family and same single owner of the JDAM name as records 68 and 77.

refute_a.reason: Although styled a ceiling increase, the paragraph names the program and its article (JDAM strap-on inertial guidance tail kits) and obligates fiscal 2018 procurement funds ($919,429,166), so it is not a §3 empty-ceiling/no-named-program umbrella; procurement money against the ammunition-procurement JDAM line, the article is the line's own, and the visible obligation exceeding the mod value points to the companion delivery order on the same JDAM vehicle rather than to a different colour of money.

refute_b.reason: No competing owner of the JDAM name exists in this index, the described article ('JDAM strap-on inertial guidance kits … for conventional inventory bombs') is the munition kit itself rather than any aircraft that carries it, and the chosen PIID is one of the record's lake_piids — the identity is unambiguous even though the action is styled a ceiling increase.

proposals.announcement_evidence: 144 Active Electronically Scanned Array radars
proposals.rationale: The AESA name matches the index rows verbatim, but the radars are 144 units delivered to 'the government of Taiwan' for installation on Taiwan's F-16s under a contract that is '100 percent foreign military sales' — foreign money, foreign aircraft. The identical name also sits on F0160P (F-16 Post Production Support), so even without the FMS problem the owner is ambiguous.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Joint Direct Attack Munition (JDAM) tail-kits
proposals.rationale: An undefinitized contract action 'for the production of Lot 18 JDAM tailkits', funded with fiscal 2013 munitions procurement funds and fiscal 2014 Air Force and Navy munitions procurement funds — the article, the appropriation and the exhibit (lexicon_doc 409, Air Force ammunition procurement) all match line 353620, titled 'Joint Direct Attack Munition'. The 30 percent FMS content to the UAE, Morocco and Norway is a minority share of a domestically-funded production lot, not an FMS case standing on its own. No other code in this org's index owns a JDAM name.

refute_a.reason: Fiscal 2013 munitions procurement plus fiscal 2014 Air Force and Navy munitions procurement funds for 'the production of Lot 18 JDAM tailkits' — procurement appropriation, procurement line, and the tail kit is the article 353620 is named for; the 30 percent FMS content to the UAE, Morocco and Norway is a minority share of a domestically funded production lot, not an FMS-only case.

refute_b.reason: 353620 is the sole owner of a JDAM name in F.tsv, 'Lot 18 JDAM tailkits' names the indexed article directly, and the foreign-military-sales share does not create an alternative owner inside this org's index — it is a minority share of the same tail-kit production lot, not a different program or variant.
